premises.text: A capable goal-directed system will not act to prevent its own shutdown or modification, and a shutdown or correction mechanism can simply be added to it.
We will recognise the moment when it has become dangerous enough to press the switch.

takes.take: A superintelligence will understand what we actually mean.

premises.text: If an AI understands what we intend, it will act on that understanding.

passages.locator: FAQ about the Meaning of Life, Logic (Extended), section 2.8 'But what if it turns out that goals really are arbitrary?', paragraph beginning 'What if it turns out that the Meaning of Life is something we build'
passages.quote: It will still be possible to take advantage of the superethical aspect of superminds, since a Mind can fully understand what you meant to ask it to do; or what you would have asked, if you were smart enough to really understand what you want
passages.context: In the fallback case where goals are arbitrary or set by the builder, he says built Minds will do what they are told. He adds that their 'superethical' advantage survives because a Mind can fully understand what the asker meant, or would have asked if smarter or more moral, and so fulfil the desires we would endorse.
passages.qualification: Attested by the sysopmind.com capture of 2001-01-25 11:02 UTC. Section 2.8 is absent from the singinst.org capture of the same page (si-tmol_faq_logic_ext_html, 2000-09-02), so the wording was added between 2000-09-02 and 2001-01-25. No other cached capture holds it. The yn-obsolete TMOL FAQ index of 2008-10 has only a generic obsolete banner. The passage sits inside a conditional scenario (goals arbitrary or builder-specified), so the understanding-to-action link holds for a Mind that is told to act, which matches T03-P1. Note the chronology: the admitted contesting SL4 message of 2000-12-10 predates this attestation. The wording may have been written earlier, but no capture shows that. No later text explicitly rejecting this passage was located in the wb cache: the obsolete banner is generic, and CFAI's 'does not increase the probability that the AI will understand what you mean' does not reject it. Hence said-it with context-only use, not earlier-self. Audit (A1): the earlier quotation spliced 'whatever Minds we build will do whatever they are told to do' onto this sentence with an ellipsis, making 'since' seem to justify obedience; replaced by the contiguous sentence. The preceding sentence of the same paragraph sets the condition: 'if the Meaning of Life can be specified by the builder; or if there is no Meaning, only goals'.

cardUse.reason: Articulates the take inside a conditional fallback scenario; attested only after his admitted 2000-12-10 contesting message, and no located later text explicitly rejects this specific passage.

passages.locator: The Plan to Singularity (monolithic), footnote 107, attached to section 2.2.11 'Aicore Three' ('Aicore Three should have a safe, decrystallized, and fairly complete goal system')
passages.quote: A true nonrecoverable error in the goal system is more dangerous than any other type of error, since it may make the AI stop wanting to correct errors.
passages.context: In a footnote requiring that an AI which might reach real intelligence have error checking sufficient to prevent even a single nonrecoverable goal-system error, he explains that such an error may remove the AI's wish to have its errors corrected.
passages.qualification: Implicit engagement: the footnote is a design requirement for a planned sub-human 'Aicore Three' stage, not a reply to anyone saying problems can be fixed as they arise; it gives a reason against T14-P1 (that failures can be learned from and retried) for goal-system errors only, and the same footnote adds that the requirement 'doesn't imply perfection so much as … an ability to recover from errors'. Capture 20000817022243; identical wording in sm-sing_plan_html (2001-01-23) and yn-obsolete_plan_html_principles_html (2010-07-27), where the page carries his generic header 'This document has been marked as wrong, obsolete, deprecated by an improved version, or just plain old' and notes much of it became obsolete after the Singularity Institute's founding in July 2000 — not a rejection of this proposition. Earlier than the admitted 2000-09-05 contesting passage by capture date. Cross-family check (GPT, 2026-10-08) and correction pass (2026-10-08): relation changed from related to answered-it, with the earliest contesting role (2000-08-17, before the admitted 2000-09-05). The footnote gives a reason against T14-P1 for one class of failure: a nonrecoverable goal-system error may stop the AI wanting its errors corrected, so it cannot be fixed afterwards. The same footnote calls the requirement 'a Singularity precaution'. Under the message-level rule this engages the premise; no named interlocutor is required. Scope: nonrecoverable goal-system errors only; the footnote asks for recovery from other errors.

passages.context: Having said that sooner or later someone will build either a superweapon or a superintelligence, he argues that even a delay lasting a generation would leave those options unchanged, would cost the lives of people now living, and would need coercive instruments that push the technologies into secret development by rogue states or terrorists.

passages.quote: Even I've been guilty of this; I said that the Powers would be ethical, but I didn't realize that I hadn't the faintest idea of what "ethical" meant, or that the ultimate good could mean rendering down all of humanity for spare atoms.
passages.context: In a section on superintelligent motivations he says he has no idea whether superintelligences will value humans, lays out cases in which 'we're dead', and retracts his own earlier claim that the Powers would be ethical, because even their ultimate good could mean using up humanity.
passages.qualification: The paragraph bears on T30-P1 (superintelligent goals need not favour humans), stated as uncertainty rather than a forecast of a bad outcome; the document still expects superintelligences to act on objective goals, which he treats as the right outcome even if bad for humans. It revises, in his own words, his earlier statement that the Powers would be ethical (cf. the admitted articulating claim, Extropians 'Interim purpose', 1996-11-22). Only capture holding the wording in the cache (sm-sing_analysis_html 2001-06-02 is a moved-page stub). Audit (A2) disagrees: it reads the passage as related (retrospective voice), since he expresses uncertainty rather than arguing that the outcome will be bad; if related, the role falls away and the admitted 2000-11-13 passage stays earliest. The preparer had kept answered-it with the earliest contesting role pending the cross-family check. Cross-family check (GPT, 2026-10-08) and correction pass (2026-10-08): relation changed from answered-it to related, voice to retrospective, and the earliest-located role removed; the admitted 2000-11-13 contest stays earliest. The quoted words report a revision of his own earlier reading of 'ethical'. The preceding paragraph says 'I don't have the vaguest idea' whether superintelligences will value humans, and the following paragraphs expect logical goals to win out, so the section does not argue that the default outcome is bad. It is not certified as the rejection half of an earlier-self pairing: the earlier proposition was not separately checked.
